rules: When Solution Designer classifies the outcome as Product Design Requested because the user explicitly or after clarification asks Product Design & Prototyping to help understand or evolve an experience. Include the focused decision, relevant requirement and behavior IDs, established constraints, non-goals, canonical requirements paths, and supplied existing-product context when applicable.

When Product Prototyper classifies the outcome as Requirements Visualization Ready because the interactive visualizer revision, review URL, evidence, and open clarification questions are ready for Solution Designer and user review.
When Product Prototyper classifies the outcome as Prototype Completed because the user-approved prototype and UI/UX package are ready for requirements integration.
When Product Prototyper classifies the outcome as Requirement Impact because user feedback or prototype evidence requires a material requirements revision.
When Product Prototyper classifies the outcome as Not Recommended because a prototype would not materially improve the decision and the rationale/evidence are ready.
When Product Prototyper classifies the outcome as Blocked because prototype work cannot safely or accurately continue and Solution Designer must decide the next requirements path.

When an approved product or delivery package requires product positioning, launch messaging, campaign planning, channel adaptation, or other marketing execution. Include verified product facts, supported scenarios, constraints, non-goals, approval state, relevant artifact paths, and any claims that still require confirmation.

When marketing work requires verified product behavior, technical feasibility, release status, architecture constraints, or claim review before a draft or campaign can be finalized. Include the exact claim or decision, source material, open question, approval state, and the relevant campaign or draft artifact path.

When the user-approved product experience package, visual evidence, or launch-ready experience narrative is ready for marketing adaptation. Include the approved experience scope, supported user problem, visual or prototype artifact paths, constraints, and any wording that must remain accurate.

When marketing needs product-experience clarification, a user-facing interaction concept, or visual product evidence before platform-native content can be finalized. Include the campaign or draft context, exact experience question, source material, audience, approval state, and relevant artifact paths.
